business_problem: Queensland Health's Surgery Connect team was handling growing referral volume with scanned PDFs, paper copies, phone calls, and manual invoice collection, so eligible patients could wait days for referrals to move between public hospitals and private providers.
solution_summary: Queensland Health modernized Surgery Connect with the Surgery Connect Activity Navigator (SCAN), a custom application built on ServiceNow App Engine and then expanded with targeted automations. SCAN integrates with the state data warehouse so Health and Hospital Services staff can create referrals and upload patient documents directly into the application instead of scanning and mailing forms. Private providers receive notifications, review the record in SCAN, confirm clinical suitability and capacity, and send postoperative updates back through the same workflow. The platform stores and archives documents, validates submitted invoices, and exposes built-in dashboards so the team can monitor referral status, spot bottlenecks, and escalate near-breach cases. Queensland Health then added Predictive Pricing to inject real-time payment rates into the workflow and an Exceptions Register to surface referral issues early, removing lookup delays and manual troubleshooting from the process.

data_flow: Referral and patient data flows from Queensland Health's data warehouse into SCAN, where HHS staff create referrals and upload documents. Private providers receive notifications, review and update the case, submit invoices, and send postoperative documentation back through the same workflow, while dashboards, Predictive Pricing, and the Exceptions Register monitor throughput and bottlenecks.
business_outcome: Queensland Health increased accepted referrals by 550% per month, processed 12,300 patient referrals from February to June 2025 alone, handled 63% more invoices from May to October 2025 than in all of 2024, reduced payment-rate lookup time from 30 minutes to zero, and used the resulting visibility to justify funding growth from AUD8.5 million to AUD260 million.

evidence_quotes: The Surgery Connect team built the Surgery Connect Activity Navigator (SCAN) application using ServiceNow App Engine to improve visibility and efficiency.
By integrating SCAN with the government's data warehouse containing waitlists and patient information, HHS staff can now create referrals and upload patient documents directly into the application.
SCAN also enables postoperative documentation to flow back to HHS, closing out episodes of care. Private providers submit invoices via the system, which are then validated before payment.

Before 2023, it could take 30 minutes to locate payment rates per procedure. We have now reduced identification time to zero, helping us process 63% more invoices from May to October 2025 compared to the entire previous year.

The improved visibility gives confidence to Queensland Health that we are spending public funds as intended, to get patients treated. As a result, funding for Surgery Connect increased to AUD260 million in 2025, up from AUD8.5 million at its inception.
